subject.title: [Feature Request] Hook Chain Integrity Protection Against Message Tampering

question: What hook-chain security model should OpenClaw support for mutable plugin hooks: host-owned audit/provenance for today’s in-process plugins, integrity checks across a future isolated-plugin IPC boundary, or per-hook permission gating first?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but implementing checksums, audit logs, or per-hook allowlists would encode plugin trust-boundary and compatibility policy that current code and docs do not settle.

options.title: Define audit and trust boundary first
options.body: Document the threat model, redaction and retention rules, and compatibility plan before changing hook runner behavior or config.

options.title: Ship redacted audit first
options.body: Add host-owned audit events for modifying hooks while deferring checksum enforcement and per-hook allowlists.

options.title: Defer checksum to isolated plugin IPC
options.body: Keep checksum enforcement blocked on process-isolation work and limit near-term work to permissions or audit surfaces that fit in-process plugins.

recommendation.title: Define audit and trust boundary first
recommendation.body: Document the threat model, redaction and retention rules, and compatibility plan before changing hook runner behavior or config.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc has the strongest recent history across the hook runner, hook types, and registry surfaces needed to carry the decision into implementation.
